rule: GOAL: Slide the purple square into the blue circle. CONTROLS: Click a nearby spot to jump the square there. RULE: Moves are capped at short distances, so you must hop step by step. TRAP: Assuming you can click the target directly from far away wastes your limited actions.

GOAL: Navigate the winding maze to the exit using exactly sixteen moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the player continuously until hitting a wall. RULE: You stop only when blocked, meaning you pass through open cells without halting. TRAP: Assuming you can stop at any desired cell; you cannot, so plan paths carefully to avoid overshooting the target.

GOAL: Drop the block onto the bar to fill the target row. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block left or right; Space drops it straight down. RULE: Blocks stack on top of obstacles and other blocks, forming solid walls. TRAP: Thinking blocks vanish after landing; they persist, so precise placement is critical to avoid blocking future moves.

GOAL: Align the arrow with the gap to clear the level. CONTROLS: Clicking the blue block shifts the arrow four steps. RULE: The arrow only moves when the blue block is clicked. TRAP: Clicking the arrow or gray area does nothing.

GOAL: Position bars to direct paint drips into three separate cup notches. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move selected bars; mouse clicks select bars; spacebar pours paint. RULE: Paint spreads across the full width of any bar it hits before dripping down. TRAP: Assuming drips stay only where the nozzle hits; they actually spread to the ends.

GOAL: Shift the white plug right to fill the gap by moving white blocks between three regions. CONTROLS: Up moves white left to right; Down moves white right to left. Click to execute moves. RULE: White blocks can only move if the source region has enough width to spare. TRAP: Assuming you must move all white blocks first. You only need enough to prevent the middle region from vanishing before the plug arrives.

GOAL: Move the ball to the target using limited clicks. CONTROLS: Click knobs to toggle their state; press the main button to trigger movement. RULE: The ball’s final position depends on the specific pattern of active knobs, not just how many are on. TRAP: Assuming movement is based solely on the count of active knobs or simple grid coordinates wastes time.

GOAL: Extend the green and yellow bars so their moving dots land precisely on the distant green plus signs. CONTROLS: Clicking a bar extends its length by three units, shifting the dot further along the track. RULE: The dot sits one unit behind the bar's end; the bar must reach length 26 to place the dot on the target. TRAP: Assuming the bar's edge needed to touch the target; the dot required an extra unit of growth.

GOAL: Clear the level in three moves. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the object; clicks interact with cells. RULE: Odd completions shrink the shape, allowing it to fit narrow gaps. TRAP: Thinking the object stays large; ignoring that parity changes its size.

GOAL: Move the tip up the shaft to reach the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip up or down; clicking cells on the panel completes the pattern. RULE: The tip must shrink to pass the charcoal collar, which is too narrow for the full size. TRAP: Believing the tip could pass the collar while full-sized, causing a blockage until the pattern was clicked.

GOAL: Align pink glyphs with blue counterparts according to the key. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; up/down cycles glyph selection. RULE: Match each column's pair to the key's specific combination. TRAP: Assuming all columns share identical glyph ordering caused redundant checks and wasted moves.

ESTABLISHED: Extension pushes beads; targets collect only when wedged against a wall. FAILED: Extending to reach floating targets; dragging targets by retracting after contact. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching a target or pushing it away from the edge. CONTROLS: Direction keys move the head; extension keys grow the chain and push objects.

GOAL: Adjust the height of five fluid columns to perfectly align with the overhead plugs. CONTROLS: Pressing a bottom button raises that column's level while simultaneously lowering its right neighbor. RULE: Every single press shifts volume between adjacent chambers, so total fluid remains constant but distribution changes. TRAP: Believing buttons act independently wastes time; each press affects two columns, forcing you to plan the sequence backward from the final state.

ESTABLISHED: Three boxes are placed at rows 28-31, columns 28-31, 32-35, and 36-39. The ghost target area is fully covered by these blocks. FAILED: Moving the top blob box to the right while carrying it at rows 28-31 caused collisions with the middle box. GOAL IS NOT: Simply stacking boxes vertically or leaving gaps in the ghost silhouette. CONTROLS: SPACE grabs or drops a box. Arrow keys move the player; carrying requires clear paths to avoid merging or blocking.

GOAL: Move the player to the green target without dying. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player two cells per input. RULE: Contact with the red block is instantly fatal, requiring strict avoidance. TRAP: Assuming the red block could be pushed or lured proved wrong; it moves independently and kills on touch.

GOAL: Fill the glowing outline with three crates to complete the picture. CONTROLS: Arrows move the worker; Space picks up or drops a crate. RULE: You must stand directly next to a crate to lift it, and face the target spot to drop it. TRAP: Walking over a ghost outline does not fill it; only a physical crate placed there counts.

GOAL: Rotate seven glyphs to match target patterns exactly. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; UP/DOWN cycles glyph orientation. RULE: Match by rotation only; mirrors are invalid. TRAP: Assuming flipped glyphs count as correct; they do not.

GOAL: Move four horizontal bars to specific target positions so they block rising columns, leaving only the intended notches exposed. CONTROLS: Use the mouse to click a bar to select it, arrow keys to slide it horizontally or vertically, and the spacebar to activate the puzzle. RULE: A bar stops any column rising beneath it. Once activated, it blocks all subsequent columns hitting its length, preventing them from emitting light. TRAP: Believing a bar only blocks the first column it touches. It actually absorbs all columns beneath it, so extra columns do not create new light sources.

GOAL: Capture the single plus by landing a shape's dot on its center. CONTROLS: Click shape sides to extend bars three units per click. RULE: Shapes block each other, forcing a specific order of growth to avoid collisions. TRAP: Assuming any path works wastes moves; only the precise sequence of extensions reaches the target.

GOAL: Match each of seven glyphs to its target shape by rotating it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selection cursor; specific buttons rotate the active glyph. RULE: Rotate each glyph until it visually matches the required pattern, then move to the next. TRAP: Assuming you must solve positions in strict left-to-right order wastes time if a better rotation path exists elsewhere.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to clear the level within the action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: Guards attack only when the player is horizontally adjacent in the same row. TRAP: Believing vertical adjacency is dangerous wastes time avoiding safe positions above or below guards.

GOAL: Transform the bottom row of symbols to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; Enter confirms the selected symbol. RULE: A two-step chain: first map the source symbol to its intermediate pair, then map that intermediate to the final target symbol. TRAP: Assuming a direct link between source and target; ignoring the intermediate step causes mismatches.

GOAL: Place four colored blocks into slots to match the target sequence shown at the top. CONTROLS: Click a block in the side palette to select it, then click a slot to swap them. RULE: Selecting a block swaps it with the slot's contents, moving any existing block back to the palette. TRAP: Believing you must drag blocks directly; you must click the palette first to "pick up" a piece.

GOAL: Place two cross shapes so their arms pass through specific dot clusters. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross three units per press; Space switches between crosses. RULE: Each cross must center exactly where its four surrounding dots align vertically and horizontally. TRAP: Assuming one press moves one unit wastes time; each arrow key press moves the cross three units.

GOAL: Rotate four colors in a cycle to satisfy slot requirements. CONTROLS: Click a filled slot to select it, then click a second slot to swap their colors. Press space to confirm. RULE: A single empty slot acts as a buffer, allowing any color to be moved into its correct position through a series of swaps. TRAP: Assuming you must use the gray palette as an intermediary; direct slot-to-slot swapping is faster and valid.

GOAL: Fill seven slots across three connected boxes with the correct color sequence to unlock the door. CONTROLS: Click a color from the side palette to select it, then click an empty slot to place it. Press Space to submit your solution. RULE: Read the colors by expanding nested boxes in place, treating sub-boxes as single units within the main sequence. TRAP: Assuming boxes are read strictly top-to-bottom rather than expanding nested structures, which scrambles the intended color order.

GOAL: Fit the small green box into the red box’s sequence so all seven colors match the key order. CONTROLS: Click a color in the palette, then click a slot to place it. Press space to submit the solution. RULE: The green box’s fixed first color must align with the same color’s position in the target key. TRAP: Assuming the small box can be inserted anywhere; misaligning its fixed color breaks the entire sequence.

GOAL: Move three objects to their matching target spots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles which object is active. RULE: Only the object under the cursor responds to arrow keys; Space switches the cursor. TRAP: Assuming arrows affect all objects or the last moved one causes wasted moves on the wrong piece.

GOAL: Build the target code by placing single colors and repeated three-blocks into red slots. CONTROLS: Click palette colors to place them; click tokens to move them into slots; press space to submit. RULE: The target code contains two identical three-color sequences, requiring a shared blue box to fill both token slots. TRAP: Assuming each slot holds only one color; ignoring the multi-slot tokens prevents matching the repeated sequence in the key.

GOAL: Match a hidden nine-item sequence using four boxes and three special tokens. CONTROLS: Drag colors to empty slots; drag tokens to the active box to reveal hidden sub-boxes. RULE: Placing a token expands its box into the sequence, filling three slots with its unique color pair. TRAP: Assuming tokens are just colors; they are structural keys that unlock hidden sections, requiring exact order to match the target list.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow block lands in the marked corner. CONTROLS: Red arrow rotates the ring one step left; green arrow rotates it right. RULE: Each click moves every block one position in the chosen direction. TRAP: Overthinking complex color patterns; the dashed box simply indicates the target location.

GOAL: Clear all pegs except one by making four successful jumps. CONTROLS: Click a peg to see valid landing spots, then click a spot to jump and remove the passed peg. RULE: A peg jumps orthogonally over an adjacent peg into an empty hole two spaces away. TRAP: Assuming any jump sequence works; you must plan ahead to avoid stranding pegs with no empty neighbors.

GOAL: Place three shapes to cover eight scattered dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches focus between them. RULE: Shapes must overlap dots completely; only isolated pixels count as uncovered. TRAP: Assuming shapes stay fixed after placement; you must cycle focus to adjust each one until all dots vanish.

GOAL: Arrange nested colored boxes to match a specific seven-item color sequence. CONTROLS: Drag palette tokens into box slots to build the pattern, then press space to verify. RULE: The game checks only the flattened order of items, ignoring which specific box holds them. TRAP: Believing box border colors must match their contents wastes time; any valid arrangement works if the sequence is correct.

GOAL: Push the block onto the marked target square. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block in four directions. RULE: The puzzle is solved only when the block fully covers the target symbol. TRAP: Believing a white flash signaled success or a locked gate; it was just visual feedback, not a mechanic.

GOAL: Place the M object into the ring target. CONTROLS: Clicking a spot moves the W object there; clicking an object swaps it with W. RULE: The M object always sits at the midpoint between W and the G object. TRAP: Believing clicks only work inside the black area; clicking outside is valid and useful.

GOAL: Move two yellow blocks onto marked cells. CONTROLS: Left/Right rotates outer ring; Up/Down shifts inner tracks. RULE: Rotations shift colors; only yellow blocks satisfy markers. TRAP: Assuming bar depletes per action; it tracks progress, not a hard limit.

GOAL: Guide two blocks to the central seam where they finally touch. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left block; the right block mirrors horizontal moves. RULE: Symmetry holds until you enter the mismatched lower rows to break the pattern. TRAP: Assuming both blocks follow identical paths; they only match until the layout diverges.

GOAL: Place matching blocks into their corresponding rings. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; clicks select a block. RULE: Each block must enter the ring matching its color. TRAP: Blocks cannot pass through walls; you must route around them.

GOAL: Match the target pattern in the highlighted panel. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle their state. RULE: The completed panel must exactly mirror the reference target. TRAP: Assuming hidden confirmation steps or complex math were needed; simple direct matching was sufficient.

GOAL: Light four specific cells to match the white dots in the target grid. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between red and gray. RULE: The target grid’s white squares indicate exactly which cells must be red. TRAP: Misreading the target’s middle-right cell as gray when it was white, causing a missed click.

ESTABLISHED: Ghosts replay recorded moves and park at their end. One ghost exists per attempt. FAILED: Multiple simultaneous ghosts to hold buttons. Single ghost replacement logic unclear. GOAL IS NOT: Using one ghost to both hold a button and clear a path simultaneously. CONTROLS: SPACE ends recording, spawns ghost, resets player to start. Arrows move player.

GOAL: Match colors to dots by moving two shapes to specific locations. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches between the X and the Plus. RULE: A shape only matches dots if its current color matches the dot's color. TRAP: Moving the X over a different-colored square might change its color, ruining the match.

GOAL: Guide yellow and orange blocks to their matching dashed squares on the opposite loop. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons rotate their respective loops counter-clockwise and clockwise. RULE: Blocks transfer between loops only when resting on the two shared central cells. TRAP: Assuming independent movement wastes time; you must synchronize rotations to swap blocks through the center.

GOAL: Place the correct color blocks to satisfy the visual patterns shown on the board. CONTROLS: Click empty squares to cycle through available colors until the pattern is matched. RULE: White marks indicate the center color; green marks indicate the opposite color. TRAP: Assuming green means "leave empty" or "base color" instead of explicitly choosing the contrasting color.

GOAL: Move two blocks to the same target square to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously; left and right are mirrored horizontally. RULE: Vertical moves are identical for both blocks, but horizontal inputs trigger opposite movements. TRAP: Assuming both blocks move the same direction when pressing left or right wastes moves.

GOAL: Reach the exit using a time-loop mechanic. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character; Space toggles between recording and replaying a ghost. RULE: Your past self acts as a solid object or switch activator during replays. TRAP: Assuming you can pass through your own ghost; you cannot, so plan paths to avoid collision.

GOAL: Paint the grid to match hidden targets revealed by three mini-displays. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle colors blue, red, orange. RULE: Mini center shows target; white means center color, gray means red. TRAP: Assuming gray cells stay empty or follow a different color, costing extra clicks.

GOAL: Guide yellow and orange tokens to specific target cells on a grid. CONTROLS: Horizontal arrows shift the top and bottom rows; vertical arrows shift the left and right columns. RULE: The four cross centers are shared, allowing tokens to transfer between horizontal and vertical movement paths. TRAP: Assuming tokens are locked to single axes; they must swap rows or columns via the shared intersections to reach destinations.

GOAL: Place two yellow blocks into specific marked slots at the top of the board. CONTROLS: Four buttons rotated two separate tracks: a long snake-like loop and a short top row, moving blocks clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Blocks moved simultaneously along their respective tracks; the top row acted as a subset of the larger loop, allowing precise alignment after rotation. TRAP: Believing the long loop alone could solve the puzzle; without using the top row’s independent rotation to shuffle specific blocks, the targets remained unreachable.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the blue figure toggles the checker/hole between two fixed slots. The green token cannot exit the yellow box; upward movement is blocked by the box wall even when the hole is adjacent. FAILED: Trying to push the token out through the hole. Attempting to connect all pieces into one group by toggling the hole. Moving the token to the top of the box to reach the hole. GOAL IS NOT: Making all pieces touch. Moving the token to the yellow box's top edge. Filling the hole. CONTROLS: Click the blue figure to swap the hole's position. Use arrow keys to move the green token within

GOAL: Guide the black shape to overlap the yellow target in the right panel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black piece; the gray figure is a mirror image. RULE: The black piece is the real object; the gray one reflects its position across the center line. TRAP: Thinking the gray piece is the player, or assuming the reflection stays on the left panel forever.

GOAL: Make all grid cells match the color shown on their corresponding mini-hint icons. CONTROLS: Clicking a standard cell flips its own color; clicking an X-marked cell flips itself plus all four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: The puzzle is solved when every constrained cell displays the exact target color indicated by the legend. TRAP: Assuming unconstrained cells can be ignored; leaving them in the wrong state may prevent level completion if they are implicitly required to match the base color.

GOAL: Insert the plug into the wall socket by aligning its red tips with the terminals. CONTROLS: Space rotates the plug; arrow keys move it across the grid. RULE: Only a 90-degree rotation aligns the vertical tip spacing with the vertical terminal layout. TRAP: Assuming 180 degrees works because prongs face down, when it actually fails to match the terminals.

GOAL: Move colored shapes to cover matching dots without touching wrong colors. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: A shape changes color if its center lands on a square of that color. TRAP: Assuming only the final position matters; the path also triggers color changes if it crosses squares.

GOAL: Move three yellow blocks to marked outer cells, then swap pairs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotated blocks along spokes or rings; one key swapped center pairs. RULE: Rotations affect all blocks in a spoke or ring, not just one. TRAP: Assuming you could move single blocks independently; you had to rotate entire groups.

GOAL: Align the black piece's white dots with the strip's blue dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece; Space toggles dot colors between piece and strip. RULE: Dots must match in position and color to solve the level. TRAP: Believing movement alone works; ignoring the Space toggle locks you out of the solution.

ESTABLISHED: The panel shows a white block touching a purple block. The canvas is unmovable. The held block and canvas are the scene's only pieces. FAILED: Clicking the canvas had no effect. Pressing at 0 degrees and 45 degrees did not create the required touching white-purple configuration on the canvas. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not to move the canvas or close the gap by shifting the bracket down. CONTROLS: Clicking swatches changes the held block color. Space presses the block. Arrow keys rotate the assembly.

GOAL: Match each tile’s glyph shape to the corresponding target shape shown in the bottom reference rows. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selection cursor between tiles; the action key cycles the current tile’s glyph orientation. RULE: A tile is correct only when its visible glyph exactly matches the target’s shape and rotation. TRAP: Assuming adjacent tiles share the same target shape; each tile has a unique required orientation.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding moving blocks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step. RULE: Ghosts replay fixed paths, pushing blocks on schedule. TRAP: Thinking you can rush; you must wait for ghosts to clear the path.

ESTABLISHED: Clearing green blocks creates open paths but leaves black barriers. FAILED: Assuming all cleared areas connect freely; some remain isolated pockets. GOAL IS NOT: A simple open field; it is a specific shape or endpoint. CONTROLS: Clearing greens removes blocks; black areas are walls; verify connectivity after each clear.

GOAL: Move the mirror strip upward so the locked pieces’ reflections align with the top yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected mirror strip; Space selected or cycled between the strip and the pieces. RULE: A piece’s reflection matches a target only when the strip’s position creates perfect vertical symmetry between them. TRAP: Believing the pieces needed to move to the top targets instead of keeping them at the bottom for the reflection to work.

GOAL: Rotate colored tiles into matching target zones using specific arrow buttons. CONTROLS: Up and Down arrows rotate the vertical column; Left and Right arrows shift the horizontal row and rotate the bottom square. RULE: Arrows perform a three-cycle rotation of their respective lines, not simple swaps between adjacent tiles. TRAP: Assuming arrows only swap two tiles fails when three distinct colors are present, breaking the sequence logic.

GOAL: Clear the path to the two dots by rearranging obstacles, then extend the sky and pink shapes to reach them. CONTROLS: Click arrows to move colored bars; click center cells to expand or shrink shapes. RULE: Shapes must grow sequentially; overlapping is allowed only if it doesn't block the target dots. TRAP: Assuming simultaneous growth is possible; the sky must fully reach the first dot before pink moves.
GOAL: Guide the tip to the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip. RULE: The path opens only after removing blockers. TRAP: Assuming the door stays closed wastes moves.

GOAL: Align the mirror strip to reflect shapes onto the second target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; Space cycled selection; Down shifted the mirror. RULE: Reflections are precise; the mirror’s center must sit exactly between the source and target shapes. TRAP: Assuming the mirror could overlap pieces; it must sit strictly below them, requiring careful spacing.

GOAL: Float the plug to the top gap by balancing fluid levels across four chambers. CONTROLS: Click chamber buttons to raise one side and lower the other; click passages to move the plug between chambers. RULE: The plug floats up as fluid rises, but only moves between chambers if the fluid levels equalize at an open passage. TRAP: Raising fluid blindly ignores the cap; fluid stops rising at pillar heights, wasting actions and preventing the plug from reaching the exit.

GOAL: Align the shrunk 2x2 tip with the shaft row, facing left, to fire a beam that destroys the red block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip two spaces; DOWN shifts rows; LEFT shifts columns and rotates the beam direction. RULE: The beam travels through aligned gray cells; only a left-facing tip at the correct row hits the target ring. TRAP: Believing the tip must enter the handle directly; it must first fire the beam to clear the path before winning.

GOAL: Grow the yellow bar to touch the blue box while shrinking other colored boxes to clear the path. CONTROLS: Click the left side of a box to shrink it; click the right side to grow it. RULE: Right-side clicks expand the shape, while left-side clicks contract it, allowing precise spacing between obstacles. TRAP: Assuming boxes are passable; they are solid walls that block growth if not fully moved aside first.

GOAL: Align the shape with the yellow zone using mirror reflections across two strips. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected item; Space cycles selection between the shape and the strips. RULE: The shape must perfectly cover the yellow target, accounting for its mirrored appearance in the reflection zones. TRAP: Ignoring that moving a strip changes where the shape’s reflection appears, leading to misalignment despite the shape being in the right spot.

GOAL: Move the handle so the pink and orange flower hubs land exactly on their matching rings. CONTROLS: Click an empty spot to teleport the handle there, swapping positions with the flower at that location. RULE: The hub is the average coordinate of all flowers in a connected chain; align this average with the ring center. TRAP: Assuming the pink flower hid the gray diamond meant it was gone; it remained part of the chain despite partial overlap.

GOAL: Move both colored plugs to their designated chambers without exceeding the action limit. CONTROLS: Click walls to toggle passages and click plugs to slide them through open gaps. RULE: A passage only opens if the wall segment aligns perfectly with the gap, allowing plugs to pass. TRAP: Assuming you can push a plug through a closed or misaligned wall wastes actions and stalls progress.

GOAL: Move the handle to specific spots so the average position of your group lands on target rings. CONTROLS: Clicking a spot swaps the handle with that location, changing your group's center point. RULE: The center is always the exact average of all group members' current positions. TRAP: Thinking you must click targets directly; instead, click empty spots to shift the average toward the ring.

GOAL: Fit two mirror-symmetric pieces into the target silhouette. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active piece; Space switched between pieces. RULE: Both the primary piece and its reflected ghost must align perfectly with the yellow pattern. TRAP: Assuming all visible dots marked the piece; hidden dots led to misjudging the exact shape boundaries.

GOAL: Reach the exit while five ghosts trace their fixed paths without colliding. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one tile; timing matches ghost steps exactly. RULE: Ghosts and player can share a tile only if they arrive on the same turn. TRAP: Assuming ghosts block you forever; they actually pass through or park, freeing the path.

GOAL: Extend the sky bar so its red dot reaches the plus sign. CONTROLS: Click to grow or shrink the bar’s length by three cells. RULE: The red dot always sits one cell behind the bar’s tip. TRAP: Assuming the dot is the tip caused wasted clicks; the tip is hidden, so aim for the dot’s position.

GOAL: Raise the left tank to the right tank’s height so their surfaces align, opening a passage for the plug to cross. CONTROLS: Clicking a button raises its own chamber’s water level and lowers the connected neighbor’s level. Clicking an open gap moves the plug into the adjacent chamber. RULE: A passage opens only when the water surfaces on both sides are exactly equal. TRAP: Assuming buttons raise all connected chambers; they actually lower the neighbor, so pressing one to raise a target lowers the path’s entry point.

ESTABLISHED: Uniform 2x scaling applies only to specific moves; middle-row knobs can trigger lateral shifts despite vertical extent mismatches. FAILED: Assuming middle-row knobs are inactive in column one; assuming top-row instructions override middle-row bits in the same column. GOAL IS NOT: A simple vertical drop or a standard single-step horizontal translation. CONTROLS: Toggling a top knob clears its instruction; pressing executes combined column commands; conflicts may nullify actions.

GOAL: Rearrange scattered gems into correct floral arrangements by matching colors and shapes. CONTROLS: Click to select a gem, then click a target spot to place it. RULE: Gems must sit on matching pattern outlines to complete the flower. TRAP: Assuming any empty space works; placing on mismatched shapes blocks the level.

GOAL: Align reflection strips and place two pieces into mirror zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection between strips and pieces. RULE: Pieces must land where their mirrored image appears perfectly. TRAP: Selecting a piece before positioning the reflection strips causes misplaced targets.

ESTABLISHED: Red arrows shift blocks along diagonal chains; the head block moves to the tail. FAILED: Assuming the chain ends at the visible diagonal; the source of the 'S' block remains unlocated. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the visible diagonal segments or rotating the 2x2 local groups. CONTROLS: Red arrows shift blocks one step along their specific path; blue arrows reverse the shift.

ESTABLISHED: White plug tips must land on different sockets; overlap blocks placement. FAILED: Nesting pieces or touching sockets directly yields no progress. GOAL IS NOT: Simply connecting the two sockets together or filling space. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift pieces; rotation keys spin them ninety degrees.

ESTABLISHED: Blocks move to adjacent cells. Leaving a cell changes its terrain. FAILED: Repeated directional presses without verifying cell-level terrain changes. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing blocks into any empty space. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move blocks one step; check terrain before and after each move.

GOAL: Collect matching pairs, merge them into a single item, and deliver it to the center. CONTROLS: Click empty dots to spawn items, click items to move them, and click overlapping items to merge. RULE: Items only interact if they are close enough to touch; distant pairs ignore each other. TRAP: Do not assume all items merge immediately. You must manually move them into contact before combining.

GOAL: Reach the open channel to exit the room. CONTROLS: Arrows move the avatar; mouse clicks dissolve blockers. RULE: The exit triggers when the avatar moves while adjacent to an open channel. TRAP: Thinking the exit opens automatically upon unblocking; it requires an active movement step to register.

ESTABLISHED: O1 must clear the nozzle band before O0 falls. FAILED: Moving O0 first or assuming O1 stays put. GOAL IS NOT: A simple drop sequence where objects ignore each other's paths. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected objects; Space confirms. O1 needs three left and two down moves after O0 shifts right and down.

ESTABLISHED: Blocks interact via push mechanics; specific movement sequences are required for positioning. FAILED: Direct upward pushing by lower blocks and complex return maneuvers for all blocks simultaneously. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the level within the initial estimated move count using standard paths. CONTROLS: Click to select; arrow keys to push or move; direction depends on block alignment.

GOAL: Move the plus shape to align its center with the target dot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the entire plus shape one step in that direction. RULE: The shape only moves if every new cell is free of obstacles. TRAP: Assuming the shape stops when blocked; instead, the move fails completely if any part hits a wall.

GOAL: Guide the 2x2 token to the yellow core by navigating a shifting grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token two cells; clicks toggle red and blue obstacles. RULE: All four cells of the token’s destination must be walkable in the current obstacle layout. TRAP: Assuming holes are passable or that the token moves one cell, causing failed moves and wasted turns.

ESTABLISHED: The panel cycles through three distinct glyph shapes with each cover action. The box only unlocks when the panel displays the specific glyph matching the box's own shape. FAILED: Assuming the panel state remains static or changes based solely on position without repeated interaction. GOAL IS NOT: A simple rotation or mirror transform that applies consistently regardless of the specific glyph sequence. CONTROLS: Moving over the cross triggers a state change in the panel; moving away leaves the state unchanged.

ESTABLISHED: The O kills if you land on it or stand directly in front of it while it moves. FAILED: Standing behind the O is safe; trying to swap cells or land on its exit point causes death. GOAL IS NOT: Avoiding the O's rear; the objective requires navigating the front-facing danger zone safely. CONTROLS: Move to adjacent cells; avoid the O's forward path and never cross its trajectory during a move.

GOAL: Deliver one piece to each of two distant target zones. CONTROLS: Clicking near a piece moves it; clicking between two pieces merges them into a new type. RULE: A click only affects pieces within a strict distance limit, forcing multi-step journeys for far targets. TRAP: Assuming a single long click works; if the distance exceeds the limit, the game ignores the input entirely.

ESTABLISHED: The robot collects items autonomously. The player moves freely but cannot interact with objects. FAILED: Attempting to manually push boxes or items to move them; they remain stationary regardless of contact. GOAL IS NOT: To physically shove obstacles into place to clear a path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. The robot operates independently without player input.

ESTABLISHED: Region A is now empty. The lock holding the cross sits at the track notch, unable to enter Region B or reach the key directly. FAILED: Attempting to slide the lock into Region B or the key’s position resulted in no movement. The level did not complete immediately after clearing Region A. GOAL IS NOT: Simply emptying Region A is insufficient. The objective is not to place the cross into Region B or onto the key’s current tile. CONTROLS: Directional inputs move the lock along the fixed track. The lock carries the cross and stops at track ends or blocked entrances.

GOAL: Guide the head to collect the final red bead. CONTROLS: Arrows move the head; the tail follows, pushing beads forward. RULE: Beads stop when they hit a wall or another bead. TRAP: Moving right too early jams the tail against the wall before the head aligns.

GOAL: Carry the cross inside the lock to the bottom-right corner adjacent to the target panel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the lock; clicking the cross inside attempts to release or select it. RULE: The lock must physically travel across the grid; the cross stays trapped until the lock reaches the edge. TRAP: Thinking the cross could be clicked to jump or move independently before the lock was properly positioned.

GOAL: Reach the red card to reveal the hidden button. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicking buttons rotates bars. RULE: Tokens survive bar rotations if they stand on the pivot point. TRAP: Assuming bars block movement everywhere; pivots are safe zones.

ESTABLISHED: The tip grew to a four-by-four block. Yellow dots funnel back correctly. The socket holds four yellow and four purple blocks. FAILED: Moving the tip up is blocked by the collar structure. GOAL IS NOT: Clearing the shaft or moving the tip downward. CONTROLS: Plus expands the tip. Yellow program teleports the tip to the funnel. Up presses move the tip vertically.

GOAL: Grow the tip to four-by-four, then teleport it to the funnel and climb the shaft. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; clicks activate the plus toggle and the yellow program. RULE: The yellow program wins if its count matches the socket’s total, prioritizing color over shape. TRAP: Assuming the tip must stay in the shaft while growing; it can expand into empty space before teleporting.

GOAL: Guide sliding blocks into matching holes using a strict move budget. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the active block; clicks select which block moves. RULE: Blocks slide until hitting a wall or another block, never stopping midway. TRAP: Thinking you can stop a block manually wastes moves; plan paths so obstacles halt them exactly in holes.

GOAL: Arrange scattered pixels to form a glowing box symbol on the wall. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character to place or remove light points. RULE: The shape must match the target pattern exactly, row by row. TRAP: Assuming you can build the shape from the outside in; start from the center to avoid trapping yourself in a dead zone.

ESTABLISHED: Draining the big room into the bottom region only lowers the level by about 1.6 rows, leaving the rise at 17-18. FAILED: Attempting to create wide drainage channels through rock to significantly lower the water level before the rise. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching a distant water body or bypassing the vertical rise limit by altering the water level drastically. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks dissolve green blocks to open channels, but cannot erode solid rock barriers directly.

GOAL: Route the lock to the hidden cross at the left edge and capture it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the lock; clicks select items to merge them. RULE: The camera scrolls with the lock, revealing off-screen targets only when close. TRAP: Assuming the cross is visible immediately; it stays hidden until the lock arrives.

ESTABLISHED: A capture requires the target to be the only item in the block. FAILED: Moving the head while keeping both items inside the wire span. GOAL IS NOT: Simply bringing the head to the target’s block. CONTROLS: Shorten the wire to drag items; extend it to capture when alone.

GOAL: Navigate a clock-face figure to the twelve o'clock pose to unlock the center. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the figure along a continuous clock-hand path, not simple grid steps. RULE: Each position has unique exit arrows; moving "backward" requires testing all keys, not just reversing the input. TRAP: Assuming symmetric controls. Left from one pose does not always return to the previous pose; some directions are dead ends.

GOAL: Paint the top half white by standing at the north spot. CONTROLS: Arrows move along the zigzag path; clicks select paint; space applies it. RULE: Movement follows the line’s curve, not screen directions, so left and right shift position along the track. TRAP: Assuming arrows map to screen up/down wastes turns; only path-aligned inputs trigger movement.
